review.decision_difference: Choose B to freeze expansion and first test whether a narrow founder segment repeatedly obtains evidence-backed X/LinkedIn shortlists that outperform manual search; advance to the existing outreach loop only if that test passes. Choosing A would validate the larger X-only prospecting-to-draft workflow immediately, reducing isolation of which stage creates or constrains value.
review.rationale: B better isolates the foundational discovery-and-qualification mechanism before outreach introduces additional confounders. Its bounded cohort, manual-search comparison, predefined thresholds, downstream-use measure, and repeat-use window make rejection more concrete and directly govern whether to continue, pivot, stop, or sequence outreach next. A is strongly project-specific and tests more of the claimed workflow, but combining shortlist quality with drafting and approval makes the smallest decision less identifiable and its success criteria less operationally bounded.

review.decision_difference: Choose A to test whether existing rules earn recurring required-check status before expanding into shared policy authority. Choose B only if the immediate decision is specifically whether centralized, cross-repository policy ownership is valuable enough to justify organizational infrastructure.
review.rationale: A isolates the adoption mechanism—required merge-time enforcement—in one qualified repository, measures genuine MCP-configuration decision opportunities, and defines explicit continue, pivot, and stop paths. Its bounded probe can distinguish useful enforcement from identity errors, coercive retention, rarity of relevant changes, and workflow friction. B tests the consequential shared-authority opportunity, but simultaneously varies central ownership, remote policy delivery, multi-repository coordination, and required-check placement, making rejection less diagnostic and increasing pilot-selection risk before rule value is established.

review.decision_difference: B determines whether the existing gateway has distinct value as a forkable component behind adopter-owned controls before expanding the roadmap; A instead tests an initial gateway-native operational-control configuration and therefore presupposes more of the production direction it is meant to evaluate.
review.rationale: B more cleanly resolves the required boundary decision using a bounded, public-information probe: independent reproduction, deterministic failure tests, and comparison against existing alternatives can reject the component proposition without assuming private demand. A tests important safety mechanisms, but introducing gateway-native authentication partially advances the production-control boundary before choosing it, while its adopter-willingness signal is not fully testable from public repository evidence alone.
